items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and translatory motion.

rubric.why: Identifies circular motion as motion along a circular path about a fixed point or centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object moves along a circular path around a fixed point or centre.

rubric.why: Identifies random motion by its irregular or unpredictable path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the motion follows an irregular, unpredictable path or has no definite path.

modelAnswer: Circular motion is the motion of an object along a circular path around a fixed point or centre.
Random motion is motion along an irregular and unpredictable path, with no definite direction.

items.followUp: Differentiate between uniform and variable motion.

rubric.why: Uniform speed means equal distances are covered in equal intervals of time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that equal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

rubric.why: Variable speed means the distances covered in equal time intervals are unequal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unequal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

modelAnswer: Uniform speed is when an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
Variable speed is when an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time.

items.followUp: Why are roads banked at sharp turns?

rubric.why: Banking means raising the outer edge of a curved road above its inner edge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the raised outer edge of the road.

rubric.why: Banking helps vehicles negotiate a turn safely and reduces the risk of skidding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a valid advantage, such as helping a vehicle turn safely or preventing skidding.

modelAnswer: Banking of a road is the raising of its outer edge above its inner edge at a turn.
It helps vehicles turn safely and reduces the chance of skidding.

items.followUp: State the principle of a centrifuge and give one use.

rubric.why: A cream separator works on the principle of centrifugal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying centrifugal force or its effect as the principle.

rubric.why: A standard use is separating cream from milk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the separation of cream from milk.

modelAnswer: A cream separator works on the principle of centrifugal force.
It is used to separate cream from milk.

items.followUp: State Newton’s third law of motion and give an example.

rubric.why: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on different bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

rubric.why: A valid example must illustrate a pair of action and reaction forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as gun recoil or walking.

modelAnswer: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and they act on different bodies.
For example, when a gun fires a bullet forward, the gun recoils backward.

items.followUp: Define unlike parallel forces and the moment of a force.

rubric.why: Like parallel forces have parallel lines of action and act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining them as parallel forces acting in the same direction.

rubric.why: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis to the force’s line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this perpendicular distance.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are forces whose lines of action are parallel and which act in the same direction.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance between the pivot or axis of rotation and the line of action of a force.

items.followUp: State the first condition for equilibrium and write its mathematical equation.

rubric.why: The second condition requires the net torque about any point to be zero; clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque is zero or that clockwise moments equal anticlockwise moments.

rubric.why: The equation expresses the zero resultant torque condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct mathematical equation for the second condition.

modelAnswer: The second condition for equilibrium is that the sum of the torques acting on a body about any point is zero.
Στ = 0, or clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.

items.followUp: How does GPS help determine the location of an object on Earth?

rubric.why: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying or expanding GPS.

rubric.why: GPS uses signals from satellites to determine a location on Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it uses satellites or their signals to find an object's position or location.

modelAnswer: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
It uses signals from satellites to determine the position of an object on Earth.
